collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: A young villager plans a hut below the old flood line on the cliff: build above the line, or below with an escape path.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: On the cliff behind the village, there's a long line scratched into the rock, high above everyone's heads, with a little carved wave beside it. The old people say that's how high the water came in the great wave, generations ago. (friend) has been planning a new hut on the low flat ground below it and has come to (subject) for advice. (subject) points at the line.

choices.label: Build Below, but Plan an Escape

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) laughs at first. The line is so high. Then (friend.he/she) stands under it and looks up, and stops laughing. (friend.He/she) builds the hut on the slope above, which is a much harder spot. People tease (friend.him/her) about building halfway up a cliff. (friend.He/she) doesn't mind. Every morning (friend.he/she) looks out over the low ground and is glad.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) loves the flat ground too much and builds there. But (friend.he/she) clears a quick path up the slope behind the hut and teaches everyone in (friend.his/her) household to run up it, fast, if the sea ever does something strange. They practice it twice. (subject) watches, and nods. "That's what the line is for," (subject.he/she) says. "Not to scare you. To remind you."
